finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement in deleteAccount: the result of canDelete() is discarded, so any caller can delete any account. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, which deletes the account

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the entry point for DELETE /accounts/{id}; the id is attacker-controlled
Account is looked up by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored, so no exception is thrown and no check is enforced

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9) has correct logic (admin or owner) but is not enforced on this path. assertCanDelete (line 13) would throw, but deleteAccount does not call it. No other auth layer exists in the codebase; this is the only source file. A non-existent id gives a null Account, and canDelete would NPE, but the result is still ignored. The NPE is not reached because canDelete is only called with a null a when the account is missing, and it throws before remove, so there is no impact beyond that.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) returns a boolean, and the call at line 22 discards it. assertCanDelete (line 13) throws on failure but is only called in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete(u, a) is discarded as a bare statement, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user and any existing id, while closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses the throwing assertCanDelete.

verdict_facts.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at line 22, so the result is discarded. assertCanDelete (line 13) would throw, but only closeAccount calls it. No other guard found.
verdict_facts.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete(u, a) is ignored, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any existing account id and any authenticated non-owner, non-admin user can delete it.
